context: Force-directed network diagram visualizing community structure using dual encoding (color + SVG texture patterns), with a grayscale toggle to demonstrate texture-alone legibility
first_impression: Principled and intentional — a colorblind-safe Tol palette layered with six distinct SVG textures makes a clear design argument, though the force layout compresses communities into a crowded central mass
what_works: The dual-encoding concept is executed with genuine craft: the Tol palette is a deliberate accessibility choice, and the legend cleanly pairs color swatches with pattern thumbnails and typographic hierarchy (small-caps header, name, subdued pattern label). The neighborhood-highlight interaction and grayscale toggle are purposeful features that serve the stated thesis.
what_doesnt: The force layout lets Alpha, Beta, and Gamma clusters bleed together in the center, undermining the community-separation story the visualization is trying to tell — stronger cluster forces or explicit spatial separation would fix this. The network also occupies roughly 60% of the canvas width, leaving the right third as dead space around the legend, making proportions feel off.
